text:
Sam: Hey team — new draft of the product launch blog is live: https://docs.redwood.ai/launch/draft-2026 (outline + benchmark callouts). Need a quick pass on three things by EOD: 1) copy polish on hero & lead, 2) benchmark phrasing (claims & numbers), 3) webinar/reg form routing for inbound leads. @Maria @Jordan @Ashley please ✅
Maria: Skimming now. Quick note — hero currently says "40% lower inference cost". Can we make that "up to 40% lower inference cost vs baseline X"? Legal likes qualifiers.
Jordan: Agree with Maria. Also need the latency numbers behind the "2x faster" line. Which model/hardware pair are we comparing? Add a footnote or link to the benchmark spreadsheet please.
Lee: For the blog benchmark we used Redwood-optimized runtime on A100 vs baseline CPU serving. Numbers are in the benchmark doc: https://benchmarks.redwood.ai/launch-2026.csv — latency p50/p95 and token throughput are there. Recommendation: swap "2x faster" -> "~2x p95 latency improvement in our tests (A100)".
Ashley: On lead routing: we want to gate webinar regs with the product-interest checkbox and map to HubSpot form ID 87654. UTM params: utm_source=blog, utm_medium=organic, utm_campaign=launch_apr26. Can marketing ops handle the form mapping? cc @legal-bot for consent copy.
legal-bot: Heads up — phrase "saves you money" requires substantiation in copy or an asterisked claim with methodology link. Also ensure privacy notice on form is present.
Sam: Thanks — Jordan can you paste the exact latency lines you want in hero/bench section? Maria can you do line edits for tone (short punchy sentences) and slot in Lee's suggested qualifier? Ashley — is ops comfortable with the HubSpot ID and UTMs?
Jordan: Suggested copy: "Up to 2x p95 latency improvement in our internal A100 tests; see methodology and raw results in the benchmark spreadsheet." Will paste the CSV snippet here if helpful.
Maria: Doing a light edit pass now. Also swapping out a long sentence in the second paragraph for two shorter ones. Will add parentheses for the qualifier per Lee.
Ashley: Ops ok — I’ll queue the HubSpot form mapping and send the webhook mapping to /integrations/hubspot tomorrow morning. Will also add the UTM defaults.
Lee: Small ask — can we add a mini-case example line: "A customer reduced median inference cost per request by 30% after adopting caching and quantized variants" — mark as anonymized and add "customer results may vary".
Sam: That anonymized line is useful for narrative. Jordan/Legal — confirm we can keep percentages as "customer reported" vs "we observed".
Jordan: I'll flag the source as "customer-reported (anonymized)" and we should avoid implying our tests produced that exact figure unless we have the log.
legal-bot: OK to use "customer-reported (anonymized)" + small-print "results may vary; see methodology". Avoid superlatives like "guaranteed".
Sam: Great — plan: Maria finishes copy edits by 4pm PT, Jordan adds benchmark footnote + CSV link by 5pm PT, Ashley queues HubSpot mapping overnight, Lee adds anonymized customer line. If all good, I'll route final to legal for a quick pass and then schedule the post for tomorrow AM. Anyone object?
Maria: No objections. :thumbsup:
Jordan: Sounds good. If legal needs more, ping me.
Ashley: Sounds good — I'll attach the HubSpot form mapping doc in this thread when done.
Lee: No objections. Small nit: can we change CTA text to "Register for the launch webinar" instead of "Sign up" — clearer mapping to the gated flow.
Sam: Done — switching CTA to your suggested text. Thanks everyone. I’ll post the consolidated copy here after edits and then @legal-bot for final quickpass.
Maria: Uploaded the edited doc snippet and highlighted the hero/bench lines: https://docs.redwood.ai/launch/draft-2026#edited. Quick reads only.
Sam: Received. I'll do a final check at 6pm PT and then hand to legal. :rocket:
